# Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos

Day 2, 13:50 · Gary Illyes, Search Relations · coverage: transcript, one-slide

Introduced by name by the previous speaker. The author's recording stops partway through the list of video SEO factors; a second attendee recording covers the rest of the talk (video factors, formats, discovery, robots controls, AI-generated images).

## Claims

- **[Stage]** Gary Illyes said images and videos drive a large amount of traffic to publishers.
  <br><sub>`D2-C523` · Day 2, Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos (Gary Illyes) · Extends [D1-C116](D1-S00-day-1-session-not-recorded.md)</sub>

  <br><sub>`D2-C524` · Day 2, Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos (Gary Illyes) · consistent with Google docs · [Google image SEO best practices](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/google-images) · Repeats [D2-C447](D2-S11-finding-the-gold-nuggets-structured-data-media-and-more.md) · Used by `DEV-IMG-01`</sub>

- **[Stage]** An image Google has extracted can appear almost anywhere Google shows results, including Discover, image search, web search and AI features, so its potential reach is immense.
  <br><sub>`D2-C525` · Day 2, Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos (Gary Illyes) · consistent with Google docs · [Google image SEO best practices](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/google-images) · Extends [D1-C116](D1-S00-day-1-session-not-recorded.md) · Extends [D1-C117](D1-S00-day-1-session-not-recorded.md) · Extended by [D3-C319](D3-S10-how-search-results-are-born.md) · Used by `DEV-IMG-03`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google supports the picture element only because a picture element must contain an img element, and that img element is what Google extracts and passes to its media indexer.
  <br><sub>`D2-C526` · Day 2, Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos (Gary Illyes) · consistent with Google docs · [Google image SEO best practices](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/google-images) · Used by `DEV-IMG-01`</sub>

- **[Stage]** One of the most reliable ways to make sure Google finds an image is to include it in an img element in the HTML; Gary Illyes named image sitemaps as the other method.
  <br><sub>`D2-C527` · Day 2, Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos (Gary Illyes) · consistent with Google docs · [Google image SEO best practices](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/google-images) · Used by `DEV-IMG-01`, `DEV-IMG-04`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google does not extract CSS background images.
  > "we don't support CSS background extraction"
  <br><sub>`D2-C528` · Day 2, Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos (Gary Illyes) · confirmed by Google docs · [Google image SEO best practices](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/google-images) · Used by `DEV-IMG-01`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Gary Illyes suggested a div with a CSS background image as a way to keep an image from being picked up by Google.
  <br><sub>`D2-C826` · Day 2, Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos (Gary Illyes) · not in Google docs · Used by `DEV-IMG-06`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's documented ways to keep a site's images out of search results are a robots.txt disallow rule (for example for Googlebot-Image) or a noindex X-Robots-Tag HTTP header, with the Removals tool for emergencies.
  <br><sub>`D2-C529` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 2, Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos · is the documentation · [Remove images hosted on your site from search results](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/prevent-images-on-your-page) · Used by `DEV-IDX-03`, `DEV-IMG-06`, the glossary term *X-Robots-Tag*</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Hiding an image as a CSS background is a fragile way to keep it out of Google: it only stops extraction from that page, so the same image URL used in an img element elsewhere or listed in a sitemap can still be indexed; the documented robots.txt or noindex X-Robots-Tag methods are the reliable route.
  <br><sub>`D2-C530` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos · [Remove images hosted on your site from search results](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/prevent-images-on-your-page), [Google image SEO best practices](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/google-images) · Used by `DEV-IMG-06`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Of the attributes the HTML standard defines for the img element, Google uses three and ignores the rest; Gary Illyes named src and alt but not the third.
  <br><sub>`D2-C531` · Day 2, Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos (Gary Illyes) · not in Google docs</sub>

- **[Stage]** The src attribute is the most important img attribute, because without it Google does not know where the image bytes are and cannot index the image.
  <br><sub>`D2-C532` · Day 2, Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos (Gary Illyes) · consistent with Google docs · [Google image SEO best practices](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/google-images) · Used by `DEV-IMG-01`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's image SEO guide calls alt text the most important attribute for providing more metadata about an image, and says Google uses it together with computer vision and the page content to understand the image.

- **[Stage]** Google uses the words in an alt attribute to understand the image, may attach them to the image at serving time, and the image can rank for concepts the alt text describes.

  <br><sub>`D2-C941` · Day 2, Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos (Gary Illyes) · consistent with Google docs · [Google Search's guidance on using generative AI content on your website](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/using-gen-ai-content) · Extended by [D3-C700](D3-S18-wrapping-all-up-ai-search-and-making-sense-of-everything.md) · Used by `DEV-IMG-08`, `DEV-SPM-05`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's Video indexing report help says only videos on a watch page are eligible for indexing, and flags 'Cannot determine video position and size' when the player is not on the page at load, for example behind a click-to-play image, asking for the player to load at its real size and position without user interaction.
  <br><sub>`D2-C942` · Google Search Console Help · annotates Day 2, Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos · is the documentation · [Video indexing report](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/9495631?hl=en) · Used by `DEV-VID-01`, the glossary term *Video watch page*</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's image metadata guide says Google Images supports the IPTC Digital Source Type values for algorithmically created images, such as trainedAlgorithmicMedia, and can show C2PA details in 'About this image', such as whether an image was created or edited with AI tools.
  <br><sub>`D2-C943` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 2, Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos · is the documentation · [Image metadata in Google Images](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/image-license-metadata) · Used by `DEV-IMG-08`</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Gary Illyes said a video below the fold is not indexed, but Google's video documentation only requires the player to be present at load, at a position and size Google can determine and not hidden behind other elements; to be safe, put the main video of a watch page in the first viewport and load the player without a click-to-play placeholder.
  <br><sub>`D2-C944` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos · [Video SEO best practices](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/video), [Video indexing report](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/9495631?hl=en)</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Do not set noimageindex on video watch pages: Gary Illyes said it also stops the video, through its thumbnail, and although the robots meta tag specification mentions only images, the Video indexing report treats a missing or blocked thumbnail as a reason a video is not indexed.
  <br><sub>`D2-C945` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos · [Robots meta tag, data-nosnippet, and X-Robots-Tag specifications](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/robots-meta-tag), [Video indexing report](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/9495631?hl=en)</sub>
